name: Real 2026
description: real programs, conferences, coaches, rivalries, bowls, CFP, AP Poll, GameDay

teams_data.TEAMS: I Believe That We Will Win!
Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field
fcs_data.FCS_TEAMS: Manning Field at John L. Guidry Stadium

Alabama: The Million Dollar Band strikes up 'Yea Alabama' as the Tide come out of the tunnel.
Rammer Jammer, Yellowhammer — the student section lets the visitors have it.
Six national titles under Bear Bryant, six more under Nick Saban. That's the standard in Tuscaloosa.
Here comes 'Dixieland Delight' — the whole stadium's singing along.
Big Al's on the sideline, and the student section is waving the shakers.
Coaches have to touch the Walk of Champions' handprints — every Alabama captain since the '40s is in the concrete outside the stadium.
Arkansas: Listen to it — the Hog Call. Wooo, Pig, Sooie!
Fayetteville gets loud when the Hogs have a lead.
The 1964 Razorbacks went unbeaten and claimed a national title. Still the high-water mark.
Tusk, a live Russian boar, is at every home game.
Auburn: The eagle circles Jordan-Hare before kickoff — War Eagle!
They'll roll Toomer's Corner tonight. Toilet paper in the oaks all the way down College Street.
Kick Six. Prayer at Jordan-Hare. Nobody does chaos like Auburn in the Iron Bowl.
Touchdown Auburn — and the Tiger Walk crowd from this morning is still hoarse.
Two hours before kickoff the players come down Donahue Drive on the Tiger Walk, through a tunnel of fans.
Florida: Welcome to The Swamp. 'Only Gators get out alive.'
Between the third and fourth, they lock arms for 'We Are the Boys from Old Florida.'
Spurrier's Fun 'n' Gun, Meyer and Tebow — three national titles in Gainesville.
Albert and Alberta are doing the Gator Chomp down the sideline.
They'll be singing 'Orange and Blue' until the stadium lights go off.
Georgia: Uga's in his doghouse and the Redcoat Band is playing 'Glory, Glory.'
Ring the Chapel Bell — the Dawgs won, and the students will be at it till midnight.
Back-to-back national titles in 2021 and '22 put Georgia at the top of the sport.
Between the hedges, the visitors don't get much sleep.
'Battle Hymn of the Bulldog Nation' rang out from the trumpet in the stands before kickoff — the lone trumpeter's a tradition.
Touchdown Georgia, and the Redcoats strike up 'Glory, Glory to Ole Georgia.'
Kentucky: The Wildcats come out to a big Kroger Field crowd.
Kentucky's a basketball school, but this football program has been to a lot of bowl games lately.
The Wildcat, Scratch, and 'Blue! White!' going back and forth across Kroger Field.
LSU: The band marches down Victory Hill. Saturday night in Death Valley.
They say the crowd here once registered on a seismograph — the Earthquake Game in '88.
Four national titles, the latest with Joe Burrow's 2019 team.
Mike the Tiger's habitat sits right by the stadium — you can bet he heard that one.
The band plays the pregame 'Tiger Rag' four-note riff again and the whole place chants 'Geaux Tigers.'
Mississippi State: Cowbells. Everywhere. You can't hear yourself think in Starkville.
Dak Prescott made this place No. 1 in the country back in 2014.
Bully the bulldog — and the cowbells, which the SEC finally allowed back in 2010.
Missouri: Tigers come out past the giant rock 'M' on the north hill.
Missouri invented Homecoming back in 1911, or so they'll tell you.
Truman the Tiger leads the team out. M-I-Z! Z-O-U!
Oklahoma: The Sooner Schooner races across the field — Boomer and Sooner pulling.
Seven Heisman winners and seven national titles. Bud Wilkinson's 47-game winning streak still stands.
Boomer Sooner on the loop and the RUF/NEKS are firing their shotguns.
They paint the Sooner Schooner's wheels red and white before every home game.
Ole Miss: They've been in The Grove since early morning. 'Hotty Toddy, gosh almighty...'
The Grove will be full till late tonight.
Archie Manning, Eli Manning — this is quarterback royalty.
The Walk of Champions through the Grove — two hours before kickoff, the players come right through the tailgates.
South Carolina: Here comes '2001' — the Gamecocks storm out and Williams-Brice is shaking.
'Sandstorm' on the speakers — the whole place is waving towels.
Steve Spurrier won 11 games three straight years here.
Cocky's out on the field — he's won national mascot titles.
They'll ring the victory bell in the Horseshoe tonight.
Tennessee: The Vols run through the T. 'Rocky Top' on a loop.
Over a hundred thousand in orange-and-white checkerboard.
Peyton Manning, and the 1998 national title under Phillip Fulmer.
They sailgate here too — the Vol Navy ties up on the Tennessee River right outside Neyland.
Smokey the bluetick hound is howling on the sideline.
Texas: Bevo's on the sideline and Big Bertha is booming.
'The Eyes of Texas' and the Tower is lit up burnt orange.
Darrell Royal's titles, then Vince Young in the Rose Bowl.
The Hook 'em Horns hand sign started at a pep rally in 1955. Now you see it everywhere.
Smokey the Cannon fires after that score — they set it off after every Texas touchdown.
Texas A&M: The Twelfth Man is standing — they stand the whole game.
Kyle Field is swaying. The whole stadium moves when they saw varsity's horns off.
Johnny Manziel's Heisman in 2012 was the first ever for a freshman.
Reveille, the collie, is on the sideline. She outranks every cadet in the Corps.
Midnight Yell — thousands of students in the stadium the night before, practicing their yells.
Score — and the Aggies' dates kiss. That's the deal here: when A&M scores, you kiss your date.
Vanderbilt: Anchor Down — the Commodores come out to a growing Nashville crowd.
Clark Lea's rebuild has made Vandy a tough out in the SEC.
Mr. Commodore — and the students who carried the goalposts into the Cumberland River after beating Alabama.
Illinois: The Marching Illini, the oldest of the big college bands, are on the field.
Red Grange, the Galloping Ghost, ran wild here in 1924.
Memorial Stadium's columns carry the names of Illinois students who died in World War I.
Indiana: Hoosier fans have filled Memorial Stadium — a sight unthinkable a few years ago.
Curt Cignetti turned the Hoosiers into a national champion. One of the great turnarounds in the sport.
The Old Oaken Bucket goes to the winner of Indiana-Purdue. The chain of 'I' and 'P' links hangs off it.
Iowa: The Kinnick Wave — everyone turns to wave at the kids in the children's hospital next door.
Visitors' locker room is painted pink. Hayden Fry's idea.
Kirk Ferentz has been here since 1999. Defense and special teams, every year.
Herky the Hawk, the black-and-gold stripes, and a pink visitors' locker room.
The Iowa Fight Song from the Hawkeye Marching Band, and Herky's leading the swarm.
Maryland: Testudo looks on as the Terps take the field.
Maryland won a share of the national title in 1953 under Jim Tatum.
Rub Testudo's nose for luck. Every student does.
Michigan: The Wolverines leap to touch the Go Blue banner. The Big House — over 107,000.
'The Victors' — the band'll play it till the stadium empties.
The winningest program in college football history, and the 2023 national champs.
The Little Brown Jug — the oldest trophy in college football, since 1903.
The Michigan Marching Band hits 'The Victors' — 'Hail to the victors valiant...'
Michigan State: Sparty's out front and the Spartan Marching Band is blaring the fight song.
Mark Dantonio's teams won three Big Ten titles and reached the Playoff in 2015.
They've been running the Spartan Walk from the Kellogg Center for decades.
Minnesota: Goldy Gopher leads the team out. 'Ski-U-Mah!'
Six national titles, most of them in the 1930s and '40s.
The 'Minnesota Rouser' from the band — 'Minnesota, hats off to thee.'
Nebraska: The Tunnel Walk — 'Sirius' is playing and Memorial Stadium is a sea of red.
Red balloons are flying after that first touchdown!
The sellout streak started in 1962. Tom Osborne's three titles in four years.
The Blackshirts — Nebraska's starting defense — get black practice jerseys. It's an honor.
The Husker Power chant going back and forth across Memorial Stadium.
Northwestern: The Wildcats take the field on the shores of Lake Michigan.
The 1995 Rose Bowl run under Gary Barnett is still the stuff of legend.
They call Northwestern the Big Ten's Ivy — and they love beating schools ten times their size.
Ohio State: Script Ohio — and some lucky sousaphone player is dotting the 'i'.
They'll ring the Victory Bell over in the stadium's southeast tower.
Woody Hayes, Jim Tressel, and Ryan Day's 2024 title. Seven Heisman winners in Columbus.
The team walks to the south stands and sings 'Carmen Ohio' with the students. They do it win or lose.
Ramp entrance by The Best Damn Band in the Land, high-stepping out of the north tunnel.
Brutus Buckeye's been the mascot since 1965. Players earn buckeye leaf stickers on their helmets.
Oregon: The Duck rides in on the back of a motorcycle.
Autzen's the loudest place in the country for its size — they built it to hold the noise in.
Nike money and Uniforms of the week — and Marcus Mariota's Heisman.
The Duck's doing push-ups in the end zone — one for every point.
Phil Knight's Nike money paid for a lot of this place, and it shows.
Penn State: 'Zombie Nation' starts and the student section is jumping.
A White Out at Beaver Stadium is as loud as it gets in college football.
Joe Paterno's two national titles. Linebacker U.
The Nittany Lion does one push-up for every point Penn State has after each score.
'Sweet Caroline' and a hundred thousand people singing 'so good, so good.'
Purdue: The Boilermaker Special rolls onto the field.
The Cradle of Quarterbacks — Griese, Dawson, Brees.
Purdue Pete and the world's largest drum, rolled out on the field before kickoff.
Rutgers: Rutgers played in the first college football game ever — 1869, against Princeton.
Greg Schiano's teams are tough. Always have been.
The R-U chant: one side yells 'R-U,' the other answers 'RAH RAH.'
UCLA: The Bruins play at the Rose Bowl. Pasadena, the San Gabriels behind it.
Troy Aikman, Gary Beban's Heisman, and a 1954 national title.
The 8-Clap — UCLA's signature cheer, eight claps and 'U-C-L-A, fight, fight, fight!'
USC: Traveler, the white horse, gallops past the Trojan Marching Band.
Tribute to Troy — the band plays it after every score.
Eleven national titles and seven Heismans. Tailback U.
Tommy Trojan's statue gets wrapped in duct tape the week of the UCLA game to keep Bruins from painting it.
Washington: The Dawg Pack is ready. Husky Stadium on the shore of Lake Washington.
They sailgate here — fans pull right up to the stadium by boat.
The 1991 national champions under Don James.
They claim the wave started here at Husky Stadium in 1981.
Wisconsin: 'Jump Around' — Camp Randall is bouncing between the third and fourth.
Ron Dayne, Melvin Gordon, Jonathan Taylor. They run the football in Madison.
The Fifth Quarter — the band plays for an hour after the game and nobody leaves.
Bucky Badger's at midfield; the band's ready to run out at full speed.
Boston College: The Eagles come out at Alumni Stadium on the Heights.
Doug Flutie's Hail Mary against Miami in 1984 — still the greatest play in school history.
The Red Bandanna game honors Welles Crowther, a BC lacrosse player who saved lives on 9/11.
California: Cal Band takes the field in Strawberry Canyon.
The Play, 1982 — five laterals and a trombone player run over in the end zone.
Tightwad Hill — fans watch Cal games for free from the hillside above the stadium.
Clemson: They rub Howard's Rock and run down the Hill. Most exciting 25 seconds in college football.
Dabo Swinney's two national titles. Death Valley rocks.
The Tiger Band strikes up 'Tiger Rag' — and the Tiger does push-ups for every point.
'Tiger Rag' and the whole stadium shaking their orange shakers.
Duke: The Blue Devils take the field at Wallace Wade.
Duke hosted the Rose Bowl in 1942 — the only time it's been played outside Pasadena.
The Blue Devil mascot does push-ups for every point... when Duke scores enough of them.
Florida State: Chief Osceola plants the flaming spear at midfield. Doak Campbell erupts.
The War Chant — eighty thousand tomahawk chops.
Bobby Bowden's dynasty. Three national titles, the latest in 2013.
The War Chant again — the whole stadium in tomahawk-chop rhythm.
Unconquered — the Seminoles' statue outside the stadium is lit up.
Georgia Tech: The Ramblin' Wreck, a 1930 Ford Model A, leads the team out.
Tech once beat Cumberland 222 to nothing. John Heisman was the coach.
'Ramblin' Wreck from Georgia Tech' — and they'll ring the bell.
Louisville: The Cardinals come out through a cloud of smoke.
Lamar Jackson's Heisman in 2016. The best player in the country that year by a mile.
The Cardinal Bird and 'C-A-R-D-S!' The Ville comes out for Saturday nights.
Miami: The turnover chain is coming out!
Five national titles. Swagger built in the Orange Bowl.
Sebastian the Ibis, the U hand sign — and Hard Rock Stadium full of orange and green.
NC State: The Wolfpack come out at Carter-Finley.
Philip Rivers threw for over 13,000 yards here.
Tuffy the wolf — a real Tamaskan dog — is on the sidelines at Carter-Finley.
North Carolina: Ramses the ram is on the sideline in Chapel Hill.
Lawrence Taylor, Julius Peppers — and now Bill Belichick on the sideline.
The Old Well on campus — drink from it on the first day of classes, they say, and you'll get a 4.0.
Pitt: Pitt takes the field across the river from downtown.
Tony Dorsett's 1976 national title and Heisman. Dan Marino. Larry Fitzgerald.
They play at Acrisure Stadium with the Steelers — downtown Pittsburgh across the river.
SMU: The Mustang Band — 'The Best Little Band in the Land.'
The Pony Express and the death penalty. Rhett Lashlee's had them back near the top.
Peruna, the black Shetland pony, races across the field after every Mustang score.
Stanford: The Stanford Band — a little chaos is part of the show.
Elway, Plunkett, Andrew Luck. A quarterback school.
The Stanford Tree mascot is a student who campaigns for the job. Every year's tree is different.
Syracuse: The Orange take the field under the Dome.
Jim Brown, Ernie Davis, Floyd Little — the 44 jersey means something here.
Otto the Orange — the only piece of fruit mascot in big-time college football.
Virginia: The Cavaliers come out to 'The Good Old Song.'
The Wahoos sing after every score — 'Wah-hoo-wah!'
At Scott Stadium the students wear shirt-and-tie or sundresses to games. Guys in ties and girls in pearls.
Virginia Tech: Frank Beamer's Beamer Ball, and Michael Vick in the 2000 title game.
They touch the Hokie Stone above the tunnel on the way out to 'Enter Sandman.'
The Skipper cannon fires after every Virginia Tech score.
Wake Forest: The Demon Deacon rides in on a motorcycle.
Jim Grobe's 2006 ACC title still stands out.
They'll roll the Quad at Wake Forest tonight — toilet paper in the trees after every big win.
Arizona: 'Bear Down' — painted on the gym roof since the 1920s.
The 1998 Desert Swarm defense. Tucson's proudest team.
Wilbur and Wilma Wildcat. And 'Bear Down,' written by a dying quarterback's words in 1926.
Arizona State: Sparky leads the Sun Devils out to a Tempe night game.
Pat Tillman played here. They still run through Tillman Tunnel.
'Forks Up' — the pitchfork hand sign — Sun Devil Stadium's between two buttes.
Baylor: The Baylor Line sprints onto the field before kickoff.
The Baylor Line — freshmen in gold jerseys sprint onto the field before kickoff, and real bears live on campus.
BYU: The Cougars come out under the mountains in Provo.
The 1984 national champions under LaVell Edwards. Ty Detmer's Heisman.
No games on Sunday, ever. The Cougars' rule since day one.
Cincinnati: Nippert Stadium, one of the oldest in the sport, tucked into campus.
The first Group of Five team in the Playoff — 2021.
Nippert's been home since 1924 — the fifth-oldest stadium in college football.
Colorado: Ralphie the buffalo charges across Folsom Field.
The 1990 national title under Bill McCartney. And Coach Prime.
Ralphie's handlers run her around the field again — five people, one buffalo.
Ralphie is a 1,200-pound American bison. She runs the field before each half.
Houston: The Coogs come out to a big Houston crowd.
Andre Ware's Heisman and the Run and Shoot.
Shasta the Cougar, and 'Whose House? Coogs' House!'
Iowa State: Jack Trice Stadium — named for the school's first Black athlete.
Matt Campbell turned the Cyclones into a contender. Brock Purdy.
Cy the Cardinal and the Cyclones' 'Sweet Caroline' sing-along.
Kansas: 'Rock Chalk, Jayhawk' — the chant is slow, and it carries.
Big Jay and Baby Jay. And the 'Rock Chalk' chant — Teddy Roosevelt called it the best college chant he'd ever heard.
Kansas State: Bill Snyder Family Stadium. The Wabash Cannonball is playing.
Bill Snyder took the worst program in America and made it a Big 12 champion.
Willie the Wildcat. And 'Wabash Cannonball' — the whole stadium leans side to side.
Oklahoma State: Pistol Pete and Bullet the horse run the sideline after scores.
Barry Sanders' 1988 season — maybe the greatest ever.
Orange Power — and Pistol Pete, based on a real Oklahoma frontiersman.
TCU: The Frogs come out to 'Riff Ram.'
The 2010 Rose Bowl champions, and the 2022 run to the title game.
Super Frog — and the 'Riff Ram' cheer is older than the stadium.
Texas Tech: The Masked Rider gallops onto the field.
They throw tortillas here. Don't ask.
Mike Leach's Air Raid — and Patrick Mahomes.
The Masked Rider's gallop again after that score — Tech's oldest tradition.
The Goin' Band from Raiderland and the Saddle Tramps' bell ringing.
UCF: The Bounce House is living up to its name.
The 2017 Knights went 13-0 and hung a national title banner.
Knightro and the 'Charge On!' chant. The Bounce House earns its name — the stands literally move.
Utah: The Utes come out at Rice-Eccles.
Two undefeated seasons and Sugar and Fiesta Bowl wins under Kyle Whittingham.
The MUSS student section — and 'Third Down for What.'
West Virginia: Pat White and Steve Slaton. Morgantown on a Saturday night.
The Mountaineer fires his musket after that score.
The Mountaineer mascot carries a real flintlock rifle — he fires it after every score.
Notre Dame: The team touches the 'Play Like a Champion Today' sign on the way out.
Touchdown Jesus watching over the north end zone.
Eleven consensus national titles, seven Heismans, Knute Rockne.
The Victory March — 'Cheer, cheer for old Notre Dame...'
The Band of the Fighting Irish marches out of the Main Building, under the Golden Dome.
Players touch the 'Play Like a Champion' sign; the leprechaun's on the sideline.
Army: The Corps of Cadets marches onto the field before kickoff at Michie.
Both teams face the losing team's alma mater first, then the winner's. The loser sings first.
Navy: The Brigade of Midshipmen marches in. Bill the Goat is on the sideline.
Navy sings 'Blue and Gold' with the Brigade after every game, win or lose.
Air Force: The Wings of Blue parachute team drops in before kickoff.
A trained falcon flies over the field at halftime.
Boise State: The Blue — the blue turf, since 1986. The Broncos almost never lose on it.
Appalachian State: The Rock — Kidd Brewer Stadium in the mountains. They beat Michigan in 2007 and nobody here forgets it.
Memphis: TOM, a live tiger, used to live on campus. The Liberty Bowl's been home since 1965.
Marshall: November 14, 1970 — the plane crash. The memorial fountain on campus is shut off every year on that date.
Tulane: The Green Wave play on campus at Yulman. Riptide the pelican is the mascot.
Rice: The Marching Owl Band — the MOB — the most irreverent halftime show in college football.
Hawai'i: The team performs a haka before kickoff.
Rainbow Warriors — and the mountains above Mānoa.
Coastal Carolina: Teal turf at Brooks Stadium — they call it the Surf Turf.
James Madison: The Dukes' Marching Royal Dukes — one of the biggest bands in the country.
Liberty: Sparky the eagle, and the Flames' fans light up Williams Stadium.
Toledo: The Glass Bowl — named for the city's glass industry, built in 1937.
Wyoming: War Memorial Stadium is the highest stadium in Division I — over 7,200 feet.
Nevada: The Fremont Cannon — the heaviest trophy in college football — painted the winner's color.
UNLV: Allegiant Stadium, off the Strip — the Raiders' home and the Rebels'.
San Diego State: The Aztec warrior, and Snapdragon Stadium where the old Qualcomm used to be.
Fresno State: The Bulldogs' 'Red Wave' — and they'll play anybody, anywhere, anytime.
Utah State: Big Blue the bull and 'Scotsman' — the students' fight song.
Washington State: Ol' Crimson, the Cougar flag, has flown at every College GameDay since 2003.
Oregon State: Benny the Beaver, and Reser Stadium in Corvallis.
Colorado State: CAM the Ram — a real Rambouillet sheep — on the sideline at Canvas Stadium.
New Mexico: Lobo Louie and Lobo Lucy — and the Pit's just across the street.
UTEP: The Franklin Mountains rise behind the Sun Bowl Stadium — the 'Picks Up' Miners salute.
Louisiana Tech: Tech the bulldog, and the Ruston faithful at Joe Aillet.
Southern Miss: Seymour d'Campus and 'The Rock' at M.M. Roberts.
Troy: The Sound of the South — Troy's band — is famous across the Southeast.
Georgia Southern: Paulson Stadium's 'Hugh' — and the Eagles' triple-option heritage under Erk Russell.
Arkansas State: Howl the Red Wolf — and the Red Wolves' 'Wolves Up.'
Louisiana: Cajun Field — 'Geaux Cajuns' — and the best tailgate food in the Sun Belt.
Western Kentucky: Big Red — a red blob mascot — beloved in Bowling Green.
Kent State: Flash the golden eagle, and Dix Stadium on a cold November Tuesday night.
Bowling Green: Freddie and Frieda Falcon, and Doyt Perry Stadium.
Miami (OH): The Cradle of Coaches — Bo Schembechler, Ara Parseghian, Paul Brown all came through Oxford.
Ohio: Rufus the Bobcat, and the Marching 110 — 'The Most Exciting Band in the Land.'
Western Michigan: Buster Bronco at Waldo Stadium, the Broncos' home since 1939.
Northern Illinois: Huskie Stadium, and the 2012 Orange Bowl team that crashed the BCS.
Buffalo: Victor E. Bull — and the UB Bulls in Amherst.
Akron: Zippy the kangaroo — the only kangaroo mascot in major college football.
Ball State: Charlie Cardinal — and 'Chirp Chirp!' at Scheumann.
North Texas: Scrappy the Eagle, and the Mean Green — a name that came from Joe Greene's defense.
South Florida: Rocky D. Bull and the 'Horns Up' sign at Raymond James.
Temple: Hooter the Owl, and the Owls play downtown at the Linc.
Tulsa: Captain Cane, and H.A. Chapman Stadium on campus.
East Carolina: PeeDee the Pirate and the cannon at Dowdy-Ficklen — 'Purple Reign.'
Charlotte: Norm the Niner, and Jerry Richardson Stadium.
UTSA: Rowdy the Roadrunner — 'Birds Up!' — and big crowds in the Alamodome.
UAB: Blaze the Dragon and Protective Stadium downtown in Birmingham.
FIU: Roary the Panther at Pitbull Stadium.
Florida Atlantic: Owlsley — and FAU Stadium, where you can see the ocean from the press box.
Middle Tennessee: Lightning the Pegasus and Floyd Stadium in Murfreesboro.
Old Dominion: Big Blue — and the Monarchs brought football back to Norfolk in 2009.
Georgia State: Pounce the Panther at Center Parc — the old Olympic stadium, later Turner Field.
ULM: Ace the Warhawk at Malone Stadium.
South Alabama: South the Jaguar — and Hancock Whitney Stadium on campus in Mobile.
Texas State: Boko the Bobcat, and the Strutters dance team — older than the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders.
Sam Houston: Sammy Bearkat, and two FCS national titles before moving up.
Jacksonville State: Cocky the Gamecock, and the Marching Southerners.
Kennesaw State: Scrappy the Owl — Kennesaw only started football in 2015.
New Mexico State: Pistol Pete — and Aggie Memorial Stadium with the Organ Mountains behind it.
Delaware: YoUDee the Blue Hen — and Tubby Raymond's Delaware Wing-T.
Missouri State: Boomer the Bear at Plaster Stadium in Springfield.
Sacramento State: Herky the Hornet — Sac State's newest chapter is FBS football.
UMass: Sam the Minuteman, and the Minuteman Marching Band — the Power and Class of New England.
UConn: Jonathan the Husky — a real husky, and the 'Jonathan' line goes back to the 1930s.
North Dakota State: The Fargodome — 'Thundar' the bison — and more FCS titles than anybody.
San Jose State: Sammy the Spartan — and the Spartans' 1939 unbeaten team.

Rose Bowl: The Granddaddy of Them All — first played in 1902.
The sun sets behind the San Gabriel Mountains. No prettier setting in the sport.
Every kid on both sidelines grew up watching the Rose Bowl on New Year's Day.
Sugar Bowl: The Sugar Bowl goes back to 1935, and it's lived in the Superdome since '75.
New Orleans in January — Bourbon Street was packed with both fan bases last night.
Orange Bowl: The Orange Bowl first kicked off in 1935. South Florida in winter.
Neither team minds trading a winter coat for Miami.
Cotton Bowl: The Cotton Bowl started at Fair Park in 1937. Now it's under the roof in Arlington.
Fiesta Bowl: The Fiesta Bowl gave us Boise State's Statue of Liberty in 2007.
Glendale, Arizona — the desert in winter.
Peach Bowl: The Peach Bowl, Atlanta's game, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Citrus Bowl: The Citrus Bowl's been played in Orlando since 1947 — it used to be the Tangerine Bowl.
Gator Bowl: The Gator Bowl goes back to 1946 in Jacksonville.
Sun Bowl: The Sun Bowl, the second-oldest bowl game, in El Paso since 1935.
The Franklin Mountains watching over Sun Bowl Stadium.
Liberty Bowl: The Liberty Bowl started in Philadelphia in 1959 before it found a home in Memphis.
Duke's Mayo Bowl: The winning coach gets a bucket of mayonnaise dumped on his head. Yes, really.
Pop-Tarts Bowl: The Pop-Tarts Bowl, where the mascot gets lowered into a giant toaster. Edible mascot.
Pinstripe Bowl: The Pinstripe Bowl, played at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx.
Fenway Bowl: College football at Fenway Park — the Green Monster in left.
Famous Idaho Potato Bowl: The blue turf in Boise for the Famous Idaho Potato Bowl.
Bahamas Bowl: Football in Nassau — the first bowl played outside the U.S.
Holiday Bowl: The Holiday Bowl — known for wild finishes. BYU's 1980 Miracle Bowl.
Las Vegas Bowl: The Las Vegas Bowl at Allegiant Stadium, right off the Strip.
Alamo Bowl: The Alamo Bowl, played in San Antonio's Alamodome.

host.name: Rece Davis
host.bio: Anchor of the show since 2015, the steady hand at the desk

film.name: Kirk Herbstreit
film.bio: Ohio State quarterback turned the sport's most-watched analyst

coach.name: Nick Saban
coach.bio: Seven national titles, now picking games on Saturday mornings

boom.name: Pat McAfee
boom.bio: Former WVU and NFL punter, the loudest man on the set

defender.name: Desmond Howard
defender.bio: Michigan's 1991 Heisman winner and kick-return legend

Tigers: Orange and black icing. It's the closest thing to tiger we're allowed.
Bulldogs: Two hot dogs, chili, slaw. Bulldog food.
Wildcats: Looks gross. Tastes great. That's the point.
Gators: Tastes like chicken. Tastes like winning.
Longhorns: Salt, pepper, post oak. Ain't no Longhorns leaving here.
Sooners: Okie comfort food, but we're eating it, not them.
Commodores: Nashville hot, and Vandy's going down.
Rebels: Grove-style, but they won't be partying tonight.
Crimson Tide: Rolled the Tide right into frosting.
Buckeyes: Ohio's candy. We're eating every one.
Wolverines: Cherries from up north. Wolverines go down easy.
Nittany Lions: Penn State's own scoop, eaten by us.
Bruins: The pastry kind. Bruins never stood a chance.
Hoosiers: Bigger than the bun. Like our lead's gonna be.
Tar Heels: Eastern vinegar sauce. Heels go down.
Blue Devils: Blue Devils. Deviled eggs. Can't make this up.
Demon Deacons: Deacons get the deviled eggs too.
Wolfpack: Wolves don't get barbecue. We do.
Hokies: HokieBird's a turkey. We ate it.
Golden Bears: Bay Area bread. Bears go in the bowl.
Cardinal: Stanford's Cardinal is a color. Tri-tip isn't.
Cougars: It's a real cheese, from Washington State. Who knew.
Cowboys: Pot of beans, hold the horse.

Buffalo: Wings, hot sauce and butter, blue cheese. If you bring ranch I'm calling security.
Memphis: Memphis dry rub, no sauce. Sauce is for people with something to hide.
Baylor: Ribs glazed with cherry cola. It works, I promise.
Pitt: a pierogi and fries sandwich bar
Sandwiches with the fries and slaw right on 'em. Pittsburgh style.
Fresno State: Tri-tip, red oak, and a whole flat of Central Valley peaches.
Hawai'i: Kalua pig and fresh poke from this morning's market.
LSU: Jambalaya stirred with a boat paddle in a pot big enough to bathe in. Feeds two hundred.
Wisconsin: beer brats and fried cheese curds
Brats in a beer-and-onion bath, then on the grill. Curds so fresh they squeak.
Maryland: crab cakes with all the seasoning
Jumbo lump, broiled, not fried, and crab seasoning on literally everything.
West Virginia: pepperoni rolls and a pot of beans
Pepperoni rolls and soup beans with cornbread. Mountain food.
Cincinnati: Cream cheese, chili, cheddar, broiled. Scoop it with crackers and don't look back.
Georgia Tech: Chili dogs and onion rings. Drive-in style, like my dad made 'em.
Kansas State: Burnt ends, and bierocks — beef and cabbage buns — my grandma's Volga German recipe.

Air Raid: Spread the field with four receivers and throw it — quick, short passes that add up, with deep shots when the defense creeps up.
An accurate QB and lots of receivers. Linemen pass-block more than they maul.
The pass-happy programs out on the High Plains.
Spread RPO: Spread out, then let the QB read one defender and hand off, keep it, or throw — run-pass options put a linebacker in a bind on every snap.
A quick-thinking QB who can run a little, and a running back who hits the hole.
The modern college default — most of the top programs live here.
Pro Style: The pro look: tight ends, sometimes a fullback, a real run game that sets up play-action.
A pocket QB, a tight end who can block and catch, and big linemen.
Old-school powers that win at the line of scrimmage.
West Coast: Short, timed throws used almost like runs — get the ball to playmakers in space and move the chains.
A smart, accurate QB and receivers and backs who are good after the catch.
Smashmouth: Line up with extra blockers and run it down their throat. Play-action when they load the box. Shortens the game.
Big offensive linemen, tight ends, and a bruising running back. Receivers matter less.
Triple Option: The QB reads two defenders on every run — hand off, keep, or pitch. Very hard to prepare for; rarely throws.
A tough QB who runs, disciplined linemen, and backs who hold onto the ball. Receivers barely matter (and won't want to come).
The service academies and a few stubborn programs.
Power Spread: Spread formations with gap-scheme power runs and a running QB — physical, but with space to work.
A big dual-threat QB, strong linemen, and a tight end who blocks.
The dual-threat powers of the 2000s and 2010s.
Veer & Shoot: Go fast and go vertical — receivers read the coverage and adjust routes on the fly. The fastest tempo in the game.
A QB with a big arm and fast receivers who read defenses. Gets you more possessions.
The run-and-shoot family tree, still alive in Texas.
